epic.title: epic-418-followon — F, F2, C
epic.intent_and_why: Finish epic #418: land the MCP front door (F, #424), get agents actually driving through it (F2, #542 + #541), then the first relocation tranche (C, #421).

definition_of_done: F: the six done-conditions in spec section F, with DC5 as the acceptance measure
F2: agents default to the door and a real dispatched agent drives a real role spine through it, measured from its own call record; the door's own rejections reach the run's episode
C: an agent at gate N does not do, plan or reserve gate N+k work; per-run delivered tokens do not grow

good_enough.mandatory_quality: A claim about what happened brings its evidence. A measured negative is a complete deliverable; an UNMEASURED condition is not a negative and is never reported as one.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: One-shot live scripts kept runnable, not CI-wired; green + independently reviewed for merge
good_enough.appetite: Rigor scales with cost-to-undo, not uniformly

hard_constraints: The CLI door stays; F is additive
No engine logic duplicated — the server wraps the engine's own dispatch
The gate imperative rides tool results verbatim; spine templates stay the single source of instruction text
settings.json is never written at user scope
Cheap fixes are routed, not implemented inside a wave under measurement
fixed_decisions: Execution order F -> F2 -> C is a dependency order, not a schedule
C's entry condition is the MCP door WORKING -- not merely built, and not merely driven once on one platform
E (#423) is out of this epic at the human's direction

current_wave.objective: Finish F2's open installer criterion, then C (#421): the first relocation tranche, against the door F2 made the default
exit_criteria: install_constellation.py ships and wires .mcp.json with an interpreter resolved per machine, so a fresh install gets the door on Windows as well as POSIX
An agent at gate N does not do, plan or reserve gate N+k work
Per-run delivered tokens do not grow
The gate imperative rides tool results verbatim; spine templates stay the single source of instruction text

issues.title: Adopt the MCP door: agents default to it for spine management, measured from the call record
issues.desired_outcome: Agents default to the door, with the CLI kept as the documented fallback, and adoption measured from the driving agent's own call record.
issues.useful_now: C relocates gate instructions against whichever door delivers them; doing C against the CLI and porting after is doing it twice.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: A dispatched agent's own call record showing door calls and zero CLI engine invocations, with Bash available so zero-CLI cannot be true by construction
issues.implementation_latitude: Which role spines change and in what order, how the acceptance run is staged, test structure
hard_constraints_no_gos: The CLI door stays; F is additive
local_unknowns: whether identity can be bound to a container the harness shares

issues.title: C: first relocation tranche — move gate-specific instruction out of the launch order and into the spine
issues.desired_outcome: An agent receives what its current gate needs, when it needs it, rather than the whole spec at dispatch.
issues.useful_now: F2 settled which door delivers gate results, so the relocation is written once rather than written and ported.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: Per-run delivered tokens measured across arms, and gate-N+k work counted from an agent's own record
issues.implementation_latitude: Tranche boundary, which roles move first, how the measure is staged
hard_constraints_no_gos: The gate imperative rides tool results verbatim
The CLI door stays; adoption changed the default, not the availability
settings.json is never written at user scope
local_unknowns: whether the tranche boundary is costly to revert once instructions move

wave_evidence.claim: C's entry condition is met: agents run the spine through the door rather than the CLI
wave_evidence.expected: The door works -- reachable and usable by an agent on the machines this fleet runs on
wave_evidence.observed: FALSE AS RECORDED. One dispatched agent drove one role spine through the door on Linux, having found the tools via ToolSearch against --allowedTools. .mcp.json hardcodes "command": "python3", which does not resolve on the repo owner's Windows machine. install_constellation.py has zero MCP references, so a fresh install never wires the door.
wave_evidence.source: Owner's judgement 2026-08-10; Admiral verification of the installer count and .mcp.json on e8d3b862

wave_evidence.claim: Role spine instructions naming the door cause agents to adopt it
wave_evidence.expected: An arm whose adoption is attributable to the role-spine edits
wave_evidence.observed: UNMEASURED. All three g4b arms loaded a skills corpus predating the adoption edits, and the accepting arm found the door through ToolSearch rather than through any instruction. Recorded as unmeasured, not as a negative.
wave_evidence.source: cold review BLOCK 4; correction recorded in evidence/g4b/MEASUREMENT.md

wave_evidence.claim: The door itself serves correctly once launched
wave_evidence.expected: A real JSON-RPC session returning real engine output
wave_evidence.observed: TRUE. initialize returns serverInfo, tools/list returns all 7 tools, a spine_status call returns real engine content with isError False. The defect is the launch line, not the server.
wave_evidence.source: Admiral smoke test on abad896d and on the merged main

discrepancies.signal: The wave-2 transition recorded C's entry condition as met. It is not met: the door does not launch on the platform the repo owner uses, and no fresh install wires it.
discrepancies.evidence: install_constellation.py MCP references: 0. .mcp.json command: "python3". Owner's box: py is an extensionless #!/bin/sh wrapper PowerShell cannot execute, python not on PATH.
discrepancies.reason: The decomposition treated a deferred criterion as separable from the entry condition it actually constitutes. C cannot be written against a door its author cannot open.

discrepancies.signal: The Admiral ranked the installer criterion as low priority by reading the owner's phrasing rather than their intent.
discrepancies.evidence: Owner's words were 'with reinstall will we start driving through the mcp server?'. The Admiral classified that as a question rather than an instruction and deprioritised g3 on that basis, then measured mid-wave that the answer was no, filed #553, and still recorded advance.
discrepancies.reason: An Admiral error for the retrospective: a requirement phrased as a question is still a requirement, and I had the measurement that contradicted my own ranking before I ruled.

discrepancies.signal: Adoption's causal claim rests on an arm that found the door by tool discovery, not by instruction.
discrepancies.evidence: All three arms loaded a pre-edit corpus; arm 3 used ToolSearch against --allowedTools.
discrepancies.reason: Real work, separable from making the door launchable, and it needs the door launchable first to be measured honestly.
